comments.author: @dm204375
comments.text: The paper you talk about from Harvard is often misunderstood.  That paper shows that models have some understanding of emulated depth information (how far or close the object is to the virtual camera).  But you cant jump from that to models understanding volumetric 3d representations of objects.  That is simply not the case. These models do not understand the images in 3d volumetric way, they only understand the various layers of an image in a 2d fashion with many hidden layers.  Those layers include things like, outline, shape, texture, depth information, color, etc.... Again please understand depth information does not mean 3d volumetric understanding.

comments.author: @terminator473
comments.text:
Regarding your point #5, according to o1, the next in the sequence is 2o. Lol.

User:
Complete the next item in the sequence:
4o -> o1 -> o3 -> (?)

GPT o1:
A concise way to see one plausible pattern is to focus on the positions of “o” and the changing digits:

4o – digit followed by “o”
o1 – “o” followed by digit
o3 – “o” followed by digit
If the sequence alternates between (digit + o) and (o + digit), then after two terms of (o + digit), it’s likely we return to (digit + o).

Additionally, note the digits:

From 4 to 1 is a difference of -3.
From 1 to 3 is a difference of +2.
Continuing a simple alternating difference pattern (-3, +2, -1, +0, ...), the next change would be −1 from 3, giving us 2.

Hence, combining both observations, the next term would be:
2o

comments.text: Let's talk about the human-AI interface... while voice seems like a likely (and fitting) approach, how about building out the interactive framework between the two sides, using human-like characteristics that both sides recognize and "understand"? I've been developing and working with what I call "personic agents", which have human-like personas, so that the personality traits of the agents act as an n-dimensional user interface for humans. So much more communication happens between me and the agents - also teams of agents - than I get from a purely tools-and-rules-based approach. And the synthesis of data coming out of those interactions - between me and the AI, as well as between the agents as they collaborate with each other - is absolutely fascinating. Interface can be behavioral, as well as 2-dimensional. It can be immersive, in fact. That's the fun stuff.
